ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Given point B on line segment AC and point D on line segment AB. As shown in Figure 2, if $BD=\frac{1}{4}AB=\frac{1}{3}CD$, and E is the midpoint of line segment AB, with $EC=12\,\text{cm}$, find the length of line segment AC.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $BD=x$ cm,\\
since $BD= \frac{1}{4}AB= \frac{1}{3}CD$,\\
thus $AB=4BD=4x$ cm, $CD=3BD=3x$ cm,\\
moreover, since $DC=DB+BC$,\\
thus $BC=3x-x=2x$,\\
and since $AC=AB+BC$,\\
thus $AC=4x+2x=6x$ cm,\\
since $E$ is the midpoint of segment $AB$,\\
thus $BE= \frac{1}{2}AB= \frac{1}{2} \times 4x=2x$ cm,\\
moreover, since $EC=BE+BC$,\\
thus $EC=2x+2x=4x$ cm,\\
and since $EC=12$ cm,\\
thus $4x=12$,\\
solving gives: $x=3$,\\
thus $AC=6x=6 \times 3=\boxed{18}$ cm.
